findings.F1: The forecast's edge is real but smaller than the cost of trading it: trades earn +0.065% before fees (t 5.98, n 26111, 53% winners) but pay a 0.100% fee gap each, leaving −0.035% per trade, and per coin-day the book makes 0.028% gross against 0.117% in fees.
findings.F2: The fee comes from the daily round trip: the position is opened on the 10:00 bar (mean change 0.48 of the book, fee 0.051%) and closed on the 13:00 bar (change 0.48, fee 0.051%). That is about 1.49 trades per day, and it pushes the book below zero in every year from 2018 to 2025 (daily −0.028% to −0.12%).
findings.F3: The 3-hour countermove at the 10:00 bar averages 0.059% (t 4.39, n 16907), and it fades with a longer hold: 0.060% over 6 hours (t 2.96), −0.013% over 12 hours, −0.066% over 24 hours and −0.122% over 48 hours (t −2.26). So the move is too small to carry a 0.1% round trip.
findings.F4: Almost all of the gain is on the long side. Longs after a 3-day fall earn +0.107% gross per trade (net +0.007%) and a +0.113% 3-hour move. Shorts after a 3-day rise earn +0.025% (net −0.075%) and +0.008%, and over 12 and 24 hours the coin keeps rising against the short (−0.17% signed).
findings.F5: The move grows with the coin's recent volatility. The 3-hour signed move is 0.005%, 0.054% and 0.113% across low, middle and high volatility terciles (10-day hourly volatility), with n of about 5590 each.
findings.F6: The trend's size matters only at the bottom. The weakest forecast quintile loses gross (−0.037% per trade). The top two quintiles earn 0.127% and 0.107% gross, the only ones near or above the fee (net +0.027%, +0.007%).

ideas.idea: Over the 3 hours from 11:00 UTC, a coin moves against its own 3-day return, and the larger that 3-day return, the larger the move against it, only while that 3-day return is a fall. The move is larger the higher the coin's hourly volatility over the past 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy only coins that have fallen over 3 days into the European midday, sized up when the coin is volatile, and would not short coins that have risen. This keeps the part of the move that is large enough to pay for the round trip.
ideas.name: midday rebound after falls

ideas.idea: After a 3-day fall, a coin rises over the 12 hours from 11:00 UTC, and the larger the 3-day fall, the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader could hold the midday rebound in a fallen coin for half a day instead of three hours, so the same single round trip is paid against a larger move.
ideas.name: half-day rebound after falls
